verifications.claim: The 2026 Masters cut rule dictates that only the top 50 players and ties after 36 holes (Friday) advance to the weekend rounds.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Only the top 50 players (plus ties) make the cut at the Masters.'; R2: 'Only the top 50 and ties after second-round action on Friday'; R3: 'the field is trimmed to the top 50 players and ties'; R6: 'The top 50 players and ties after the first two rounds'; R7: 'The Top 50 and ties will make the cut'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the current rule as top 50 and ties after 36 holes.

verifications.claim: The previous rule included any player within 10 strokes of the leader.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Before the rule change, any player within 10 strokes of the leader after 36 holes advanced'; R2: 'those within 10 strokes of the leader'; R3: 'anyone within 10 shots of the lead also advanced'; R7: 'any player who was within 10 shots of the leader after 36 holes'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe the prior rule including players within 10 strokes of the leader.

verifications.claim: The previous rule is no longer in effect.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'This rule was put into effect during the 2020 Masters' (new top 50 only); R2: 'Beginning in 2020, the lowest 50 and ties qualify'; R3: 'but that is no longer the case'; R7: 'Before the 2020 Masters, however, that rule was eliminated'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm the 10-stroke rule ended in 2020 and is no longer used.
